Cause: The api-gateway pods in the edge namespace mount the gateway-limits ConfigMap using a subPath (mountPath /etc/gateway/limits.yaml, subPath limits.yaml). Containers that consume a ConfigMap via a subPath volume mount do not receive updates when the ConfigMap changes [cite: concepts/configuration/configmap#using-configmaps-as-files-from-a-pod-4][cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-pod-configmap#mounted-configmaps-are-updated-automatically-0]. Both pods (api-gateway-7c9f8d6b54-x2kqp and -r7tmw) started 2026-05-21 06:02, well before the 09:10 ConfigMap edit, so they are still enforcing the old 100 rps limit — hence acme-logistics is still getting 429s.

Fix (owner action): Roll the api-gateway deployment in the edge namespace so new pods pick up the updated ConfigMap, e.g. `kubectl -n edge rollout restart deploy/api-gateway` and then `kubectl -n edge rollout status deploy/api-gateway`. To avoid needing a restart on future limit changes, drop the subPath and mount the ConfigMap as a directory (e.g. mountPath /etc/gateway with the file projected as limits.yaml); non-subPath ConfigMap volume mounts are updated automatically, subject to the kubelet sync period + cache TTL delay [cite: concepts/configuration/configmap#using-configmaps-as-files-from-a-pod-2][cite: tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-pod-configmap#mounted-configmaps-are-updated-automatically-0].
